doc.title: Scott Robinson interviewed by Monk Rowe,Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Pre-interview chat: embarrassing sets and a musician's dream
summary: Robinson jokes about a rough first tune and recounts a recurring anxiety dream of being late to a symphony; Rowe opens the filming.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: It got better. I couldn’t play anything on the first tune, it was embarrassing. But it happens sometimes. Music can be embarrassing. It’s like dropping your drawers every time you get up you know.
You wouldn’t believe the dreams that musicians have. Are you a musician?

Okay well then you probably have had them all. I had one recently where I was late on stage to play with a big orchestra, a big symphony orchestra. And I was late and I realized oh, man, I’m supposed to be on stage. And I got my horn and I got to the side of the stage and then I realized I don’t have my tie on — I’m in a tuxedo with no tie. So I find my tie and I put the thing on and I’m like oh, man, and I go out on the stage and the orchestra is playing already, right? And the conductor is going like this. And I just walk out on the stage and I’m like where am I supposed to sit? And I’m stepping through the violins and the violas, like looking around for my stand, and where am I supposed to sit — like in front of the whole audience you know, it’s really, really embarrassing. I couldn’t find any saxophones anywhere. Where am I? And then finally I looked back in the other wing, and I saw a saxophone player. So I got all the way over to him, and I went crashing through the whole orchestra, to the other side of the stage, and I went up and I said “where are the saxophones sitting?” And he said, “We’re not on until the Ellington.”
Was the camera rolling on that? Yeah, well, we may splice that in at the end. Good story. I hope it’s not a harbinger of things to come. © Hamilton Fillius Archive -2-
We’re filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive today in Chautauqua, New York, and I’m pleased to have Scott Robinson, saxophonist, with us. Welcome.
You just got off a pretty hot set downstairs with some good competition.
